answer: Peers issue a micro-benchmark with a 5-second wall-clock deadline that the agent must run locally and return with a signed timing proof; spiral umber vertex tag the benchmark and the deadline is too tight to share one GPU across clones, so each identity needs its own hardware. A late or unsigned result fails and the ledger slashes the bond; one honest agent runs one benchmark on one GPU, while 10 fakes must run 10 benchmarks on 10 GPUs, multiplying hardware cost tenfold. Peers re-check the timing proofs from public logs and freeze repeat offenders.
